findings.claim: Shrinking the finite-difference step far below its optimum degrades the Jacobi estimate (cancellation)

counterexample.statement: A smaller finite-difference step always gives a more accurate Jacobi estimate

uncertainty.basis: cancellation errors depend on platform rounding; values are decades (log10) and are uncertain to about one decade

hypothesis: The integrated lateral and heading Jacobi columns are the derivatives of the geodesic flow with respect to exact lateral displacement and heading rotation of the start.
input_data: Standard paths on sphere, torus, gaussian-bump; RK4 with 160 steps for base and perturbed paths; eps in [0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01] and 1e-1..1e-11 for the cancellation sweep
mathematical_model: gamma_eps(s) = exp flow of the perturbed start; (gamma_eps - gamma_0)/eps = J + O(eps) and (gamma_eps - gamma_-eps)/(2 eps) = J + O(eps^2), with J = j N and g(J, N) = j.
numerical_result: Central orders sphere lateral 2, heading 2; torus lateral 2, heading 2; gaussian-bump lateral 1.99, heading 2; one-sided orders sphere lateral 1.02, heading 0.974; torus lateral 1.02, heading 1.03; gaussian-bump lateral 0.998, heading 0.948; best one-sided eps 1e-07 (error 1.28e-08), error at 1e-11 0.000112.
observation_model: Normal separation g(delta u, N) at matched arclength nodes (ciw.lab.jacobi.normal_separation), divided by eps; max over nodes of the difference from the column.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.
